# Owner Golden Handoff

This is the single evidence drop area. Do not create another versioned intake
tree. The complete current request is in [`TODO.md`](TODO.md).

## Evidence labels

- **Owner-provided source:** a file supplied from the official project/build
  flow. Its original technical filename and provenance are retained.
- **Derived replay fixture:** a file sliced or generated by repository tooling
  from an owner-provided source. It is useful for deterministic replay, but it
  is not an independently supplied product replacement BIN.
- **Independent reference output:** the complete final firmware produced by
  the approved legacy Postbuild/Combiner flow, independently of the V2 tool.
- **Direct product golden:** one same-run set containing the official base,
  actual replacement inputs, independent reference output, and execution
  provenance. This is stronger than a self-replacement replay fixture.

The committed NT51926 and NT51927 bases are owner-provided sources. Their
committed CtrlRAM input files are derived replay fixtures sliced from those
bases; they were not supplied as separate product replacement BINs.

## Firmware stage names

Do not compare files from different stages as if they were the same golden:

| Canonical name | Stage |
| --- | --- |
| `compile.bin` | Raw compiler/linker output before Postbuild. A Copy Header window may still contain its linker fill such as `0xFF` or `0x00`. |
| `base.bin` | Released/reference firmware used as the immutable Replace base. It may already contain a Copy Header written by an earlier Postbuild. |
| `replace-pre-combiner.bin` | Base after declared replacement operations but before Legacy Combiner header/CRC processing. |
| `expected.bin` | Complete final output after the approved legacy Postbuild and Legacy Combiner command sequence. This is the final golden oracle. |

The main Header CRC and Copy Header CRC inside one valid final image may differ
because the legacy command copies the header before refreshing the source CRC.
For the inspected NT51926 Common FW 1.4.1 base, source Header `[0x00000,0x00100)`
and Copy Header `[0x32F50,0x33050)` differ only at the two four-byte CRC words
`[+0x1C,+0x20)` and `[+0xFC,+0x100)`.

This stage difference does not relax the golden gate: the complete V2 plus
approved external-Combiner output must match the same-stage `expected.bin`
byte-for-byte. A raw `compile.bin` is not an acceptable substitute for
`expected.bin`.

## Drop rules

- Use the existing workflow/IC/case folders listed in `TODO.md`.
- Keep original technical project/product identifiers and filenames. If files
  are renamed to the canonical drop names, tell us the original names.
- For one case, all files must come from the same reference execution. Do not
  mix a base, replacement inputs, and output from different builds.
- Incoming payloads remain ignored while unreviewed. After byte, hash,
  provenance, privacy, and firmware-owner review, accepted replay inputs and
  outputs are committed under `testdata/golden/<workflow>/` with a manifest.
- Remove personal names, emails, account ids, home/user-profile paths, and
  document author metadata. Retain project and product information.
- Do not resend an already pinned tool. Do not commit credentials, signing
  material, licensed tools, or unrelated archives.
- Evidence intake never promotes runtime support by itself.

## Information needed with every direct case

You may provide this information in a short text note or in chat; you do not
need to author JSON manually:

- IC and single/cascade/chip-count mode;
- Common FW/profile version;
- source archive, build, or ticket identifier without personal information;
- original base, replacement-input, and output filenames;
- whether the output is the final file after Postbuild and Legacy Combiner;
- exact command/log only when it differs from the repository-pinned command;
- firmware-owner approval scope: byte evidence only, alias scope, or runtime
  promotion review.

Repository intake calculates file sizes and SHA-256 hashes.
